prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a low-speed head-on collision. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1260; do not mention it.)
text:
This firm represents the injured party in connection with the motor vehicle collision involving your insured. Our client was injured in a head-on collision at low speed and is now receiving treatment for those injuries. Please direct all further communication regarding this matter to this office and do not contact our client directly, either by telephone, in writing, or in person.

We ask that you provide a certified copy of the declarations page for the policy in force at the time of the collision, together with a statement of the bodily injury and property damage liability limits applicable to this loss. Please also confirm whether any other coverage, including excess or umbrella coverage, may apply.

Your insured and your company are hereby placed on notice to preserve all evidence relating to this collision. This includes vehicle and event data recorder information, photographs, repair and salvage records, witness statements, recorded calls, claim file materials, and any dash camera or telematics data. Any destruction or alteration of such evidence may result in claims for spoliation.

We look forward to your prompt written response.
